text:
mira: FYI we started seeing a latency delta on attention path after the kernel-selector rollout this morning. p95 up ~2x for some seq/batch combos. filing here before I forget.

dan: which kernel variants are being chosen now vs before? flash_paged -> flash_fused or the other way around?

mira: selector moved certain cases to the new paged-flash path. before: flash_fused for small batches, now paged_flash for batch=1..4 when KV cache present. repro numbers below.

arya: can you paste the microbench output? even a single-run comparison helps.

mira: sure — reproduced on canary: model=llama-2-13b, seq=512, batch=1
```
# before (stable): kernel=flash_fused  p50=12.3ms  p95=41.7ms  p99=112.0ms
# after (canary): kernel=paged_flash  p50=18.8ms  p95=95.2ms  p99=174.6ms
```

perf-bot: quick-run perf harness (10 iters) attached:
```
2026-02-20 09:12:01 model=llama2-13b seq=512 batch=1 kernel=paged_flash avg=22.1ms p95=98.3ms p99=168.9ms
2026-02-20 09:12:15 model=llama2-13b seq=512 batch=1 kernel=flash_fused avg=13.0ms p95=42.0ms p99=110.5ms
```

kevin: sounds like paged_flash has overheads on small KV hits — could be additional prefetch / stride logic or extra kernel launch overhead. did we see CPU prep time change?

mira: traced with our lightweight tracer. two hotspots: (1) kv cache lookup + rehydrate cost (~6-10ms extra on first token) (2) an extra cudaStreamSynchronize path in paged kernel selection. snippet:
```
TRACE: kv.lookup: 0.7ms -> 7.3ms
TRACE: prepare_kv_prefetch: 0.2ms -> 6.1ms
TRACE: kernel_launch(paged): 0.6ms -> 3.8ms
TRACE: total extra ~13.5ms
```

jen: interesting. could be selector enabling prefetch when it shouldn't for warm-KV. any change in batching heuristics? e.g., preferring per-request prefetch vs shared prefetch?

mira: yes, selector flip also toggled `enable_prefetch=true` for paged_flash by default. previous fused path used lazy-prefetch.

arya: quick experiment idea: force paged_flash but disable prefetch, and also force fused with prefetch enabled — helps isolate whether prefetch or kernel itself is main culprit.

kevin: I ran that locally:
```
# canary node
> kernel=paged_flash prefetch=off  p95=46ms p99=120ms
> kernel=paged_flash prefetch=on   p95=96ms p99=170ms
> kernel=flash_fused prefetch=on  p95=42ms p99=115ms
```

mira: that suggests prefetch policy is the dominant factor. paging + aggressive prefetch = worse latency for small batches.

dan: actionable options: revert selector change, or patch selector to keep prefetch off for batch<=4/seq<=1024, or change prefetch to be async w/o sync points. Which is fastest to deploy?

kevin: fastest is a selector patch that adds a guard: "if batch<=4 && seq<=1024 -> prefer flash_fused OR set prefetch=false for paged". I can open a small PR and run canary.

mira: please do. also let's add a perf regression test to the nightly matrix covering these (model, seq=512, batch=1..4) to catch this.

jen: opened GH PR #4128 gating prefetch on small batches, added a regression test job. tagging @kevin for review.

perf-bot: perf ci run queued: job=regression-small-batches-llama2-13b seq=512 batch=1..4

arya: follow-up: we should audit selector logic for other side-effects (e.g., extra stream syncs). also document default prefetch policy in the kernel selection README.

mira: agreed. assigning follow-ups: kevin -> selector guard PR, jen -> add nighttime e2e harness monitoring, dan -> audit stream sync points in paged kernel. I'll monitor canary once PR lands. :thumbsup:
